query.scope: worldwide, single request (no bounding-box split needed)
query.notes: Worldwide query returned in ~60s with no timeout/429/remark. Splitting by scheme or bounding box was not required.

processing.coordinate_rule: node -> lat/lon directly; way/relation -> Overpass 'center' (centroid) coordinates from 'out center tags' output
processing.country_derivation: Cheap only: used OSM tags.addr:country verbatim where tagged (240 / 4530 raw elements, ~5.3% coverage). No reverse-geocoding was run against the other ~95%, per instructions not to geocode every point. US/non-US totals in this file are instead computed by bounding-box classification (see below), which is independent of the sparse addr:country tag.
extra_cheap_fields_kept_in_meta: ref (OSM ref tag, e.g. facility code)
osm_tag (which of the two tag schemes matched)
osm_id (type/id, for traceability back to OSM)

dedup_rule.text: Same name (case-insensitive) within ~200m of each other, OR any two unnamed points within ~50m of each other -> collapsed to one record.
dedup_rule.implementation: Haversine great-circle distance; spatial grid index (0.01-degree cells, ~1.1km) used to bound neighbor search instead of full O(n^2) comparison. Within a duplicate pair, the record with richer metadata (has name > has operator > more meta keys) was kept.

brockovich_merge_pass.additional_heuristic: A Brockovich point was also treated as a duplicate of an existing OSM point if they were within 200m AND one operator/company string was a substring of the other (handles e.g. 'Amazon' vs 'Amazon Web Services' naming drift across sources).
brockovich_merge_pass.observation: Zero overlap detected between the Brockovich hyperscale/AI list and the OSM dataset. This is plausible, not suspicious: OSM's telecom=data_center / building=data_center tagging is dominated by manually-surveyed classic colocation/telecom facilities (Equinix, Digital Realty, NTT, CyrusOne, etc.), while Brockovich's list is specifically 2024-2026 hyperscale AI-training campuses (xAI Colossus, Stargate sites, new Meta/Google/Microsoft AI buildouts) that are largely too new, too remote, or too recently announced to have been mapped into OSM yet. Manually spot-checked the Ashburn/Loudoun County cluster (both sources are dense there): the two datasets' points for that area are legitimately distinct buildings/operators sitting only ~130m-3km apart, not the same facility double-counted.

us_bbox_definition.caveat: Rough rectangular boxes, not a real US/Canada/Mexico border. A handful of points in northern Mexico or southern Canada near the border could be misclassified. Chosen for cheapness per instructions rather than a polygon-in-country test.

enrichment_attempt.description: US-focused community accountability map (Erin Brockovich initiative) tracking major/hyperscale AI data centers plus crowd-sourced 'issue' reports.
enrichment_attempt.how_found: Page HTML fetched directly; the map's own two fetch() JSON endpoints (community-reports.json, zip-geocodes.json) turned out to be the *complaint* pins, not the facility list. The actual data-center markers are an inline JavaScript literal array (`var centers = [...]`, ~140 entries) embedded directly in the page's <script> block, extracted with Node.js by isolating and evaluating that static array literal (no external calls, no execution of page logic beyond parsing the data structure) and dumping it to JSON.
enrichment_attempt.inclusion_decision: Only 'operational' and 'construction' entries (98 total) were merged in. 'proposed' entries (42) were excluded — per Brockovich's own legend these are 'in pipeline / pending approval' with no physical footprint yet, which conflicts with this layer's 'REAL data-center locations' / 'no fabricated records' mandate. A proposal is not yet a place where the cloud touches ground.
fields_captured_in_meta: citation (their own cited press/source list per point)

caveats: OSM completeness bias: OpenStreetMap coverage of data centers is driven entirely by volunteer mapping effort. Countries/regions with active OSM communities and mapping parties (much of Europe, US, parts of East Asia/Oceania) are almost certainly over-represented relative to their true share of global data-center capacity; regions with sparse OSM editing (much of Africa, Central Asia, parts of Latin America and the Middle East) are almost certainly under-represented. The counts here reflect 'what's been mapped', not 'what exists'.

Tag ambiguity: this query is intentionally literal. It picked up at least one 'man_made=tower' co-tagged with 'telecom=data_center' (a comms tower, not a building) and general 'building=data_center' polygons whose companion 'building:levels'/'building:colour' tags suggest ordinary office buildings mis-tagged or shared with unrelated functions (e.g. one relation tagged 'building=office' with a data-center-adjacent name). No manual curation/removal was performed beyond the specified dedup rule -- the dataset is exactly what the two tag schemes return.

Way/relation centroids ('out center') are geometric centers of the mapped building footprint, not necessarily the coordinates of any specific rack room or entrance; for large campuses (e.g. multi-building hyperscale sites) this can land the point anywhere within the polygon.

addr:country coverage is sparse (~5%) in the raw OSM data, so per-point 'country' in meta is present for only a minority of OSM-derived records. The 4530/4244/4342 totals and the reported US share come from a rough bounding-box test, not a verified country field on every record.

Multi-building corporate campuses can appear as several adjacent OSM points (visible in the Ashburn/Loudoun County cluster) that are legitimately distinct buildings, not un-caught duplicates -- but a human glancing at the map may perceive apparent clustering as noise rather than the real density of that specific corridor.

Brockovich source is a community/advocacy project, not an official registry; its 'operational'/'construction' status labels and coordinates are as accurate as its own citations (press articles, filings) and it explicitly states 'location data may be approximate' and that smaller/unannounced facilities are not listed. It is US-only, so it does not affect non-US coverage or bias.

This snapshot is a point-in-time capture (retrieved 2026-07-06). Both OSM and the Brockovich list change continuously (new construction, demolitions, editor corrections); no attempt was made to validate against a third source.
